lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Um, actually, it's two thousand four hundred and seventy-five. Delta counts every one, and so do I.
lines.script: [correcting] Um actually it's Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five. [reminding doting] Delta counts every one... [slowly, admitting with guilt] and so do I.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: How many SkyMiles is that now?
lines.script: [skeptical] How many SkyMiles is that now?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Four hundred and twelve thousand.
lines.script: [proud, precise] Four hundred and twelve THOUSAND.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe! What are you saving them for?
lines.script: [amused annoyed] Babe! What are you SAVING them for?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Something really special.
lines.script: [dreamy, hushed] Something really special.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You said that at three hundred thousand.
lines.script: [slightly skeptical] You said that at [emphasized]THREE [normal] hundred thousand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It has to be REALLY special. But I'd have flown here for zero miles.
lines.script: [defensive] It has to be REALLY special. [warm, softly] But I'd have flown here for zero miles.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Zero miles. Babe. That's the most romantic thing a Delta person can say.
lines.script: [touched] Zero miles. Babe. [sarcastic] That's the most romantic thing a Delta person can say.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Wait, why is the sky PURPLE? It's two in the afternoon!
lines.script: [alarmed] Wait, why is the sky [disbelief] PURPLE? [trailing, puzzled] It's two in the afternoon!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's been like that since this morning. I held my soda up to it. It's the exact same color.
lines.script: [resigned, nonchalant] It's been like that since this morning. [investigating] I held my soda up to it. [pleasantly surprised] It's the EXACT same color.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I don't know what it is, babe. But it's pretty grape.
lines.script: [nonchalant] I don't know what it is, babe. [punchline] But it's pretty GRAPE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Don't make me laugh, it's freaky! ...Okay. It IS a little grape.
lines.script: [anxious, amused] Don't make me laugh, it's freaky! [admitting] ...Okay. [agreeing] It IS a little grape.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Something strange happened on Long Island too. A blob of mud with eyes climbed in my mother's kitchen window and ran off with her rhubarb crisp.
lines.script: [bursting to tell] Something strange happened on Long Island too. [storytelling, building] A blob of mud with EYES climbed in my mother's kitchen window [scandalized] and ran off with her rhubarb crisp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The mud took Deedee's crisp? Is the mud okay?
lines.script: [genuinely concerned] The mud took Deedee's crisp? [sincere, worried] Is the mud okay?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We chased it to the pond. And there was a talking fish as big as a car, wearing her baking tin like a crown.
lines.script: [storytelling] We chased it to the pond. [amazed, building] And there was a talking fish as big as a CAR, [savoring the detail] wearing her baking tin like a crown.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: A talking fish! What did he say?
lines.script: [delighted] A talking fish! [eagerly curious] What did he SAY?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He said "Glub." Then he gave Rose a gold coin.
lines.script: [setting it up] He said... [flat, deadpan] "Glub." [proud uncle] Then he gave Rose a gold coin.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Mud in the kitchen, a talking fish, and now a purple sky. Babe, something fishy is going on.
lines.script: [tallying, nonchalant] Mud in the kitchen, a talking fish, and now a purple sky. [punchline] Babe, something FISHY is going on.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The fish was the nicest part!
lines.script: [defending the fish] The fish was the NICEST part!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I want to go look at that sky with you. But first I have to feed Bready Mercury. He's been alone for a week.
lines.script: [sweet] I want to go look at that sky with you. [guilty, fussing] But first I have to feed Bready Mercury. [doting] He's been alone for a WEEK.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He hasn't been alone. Come on, I'll show you.
lines.script: [knowing, teasing] He hasn't been alone. [inviting] Come on, I'll show you.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: So I stayed here with her. I was coming over anyway. I've been feeding Bready Mercury every day.
lines.script: [casual] So I stayed here with her. [downplaying] I was coming over anyway. [quietly proud] I've been feeding Bready Mercury every day.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every day? Fifty grams of flour and fifty grams of water?
lines.script: [touched] Every DAY? [nit picky, checking] Fifty grams of flour and fifty grams of water?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Fifty and fifty. I used your little scale.
lines.script: [patient, reassuring] Fifty and fifty. [amused] I used your little scale.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He got so big he was climbing out of the jar. So I baked a loaf with him.
lines.script: [amused] He got SO big he was climbing out of the jar. [nonchalant] So I baked a loaf with him.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's perfectly round! How did you get it so round?
lines.script: [astonished] It's PERFECTLY round! [nit picky, curious] How did you get it so round?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I shaped it on my pottery wheel.
lines.script: [nonchalant, proud] I shaped it on my pottery wheel.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: On the pottery wheel! That's brilliant. Why have I been doing it with my hands?
lines.script: [mind blown] On the pottery wheel! [admiring] That's brilliant. [realizing, dismayed] Why have I been doing it with my HANDS?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I make bowls all day, babe. So I made you a bread bowl.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I make bowls all day, babe. [punchline] So I made you a BREAD bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A bread bowl! Now we need soup.
lines.script: [thrilled] A bread bowl! [suddenly businesslike] Now we need soup.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara, sit.
lines.script: [firm, loving] Nara, sit.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Paw.
lines.script: [firm, loving] Paw.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He's twice as big as when I left! What have you been doing with him?
lines.script: [astonished] He's TWICE as big as when I left! [playfully suspicious] What have you been doing with him?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I sing to him while I stir. He's Bready Mercury. He needs his music.
lines.script: [nonchalant] I sing to him while I stir. [stating the obvious] He's Bready Mercury. [dead serious] He NEEDS his music.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Which songs?
lines.script: [intrigued] Which songs?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: "Another One Bites the Crust."
lines.script: [deadpan] "Another One Bites the... [punchline] CRUST."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "Don't Stop Me Dough!"
lines.script: [delighted, singing along] "Don't Stop Me DOUGH!"

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. That's so good. I'm singing that one tomorrow.
lines.script: [impressed] Babe. [admiring] That's SO good. [nonchalant] I'm singing that one tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's the same purple as the sky! An hour ago it was way up on the hill. Now it's on my lawn!
lines.script: [alarmed] That's the same purple as the sky! [working it out] An hour ago it was way up on the hill. [panicking] Now it's on my LAWN!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington is sitting out on his porch in that. Come on!
lines.script: [worried, urgent] Mr. Washington is sitting out on his porch in that. [urging] Come ON!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: What happened in 1979?
lines.script: [gentle, humoring] What happened in 1979?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He just said the same thing again, word for word.
lines.script: [unsettled] He just said the same thing again... [creeped out] word for word.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He always finishes that story. I've heard it nine times. It ends with gumbo.
lines.script: [fond] He ALWAYS finishes that story. [nonchalant] I've heard it nine times. [worried] It ends with gumbo.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's not a nice afternoon, Mr. Washington! The air is purple!
lines.script: [pleading, polite] It's NOT a nice afternoon, Mr. Washington! [alarmed] The air is purple!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. That cloud has a face. And it just talked to us.
lines.script: [rattled, hushed] Babe. That cloud has a face. [disbelief] And it just TALKED to us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's like the mud at my mother's house! I told you they talk!
lines.script: [vindicated] It's like the mud at my mother's house! [triumphant] I TOLD you they talk!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You did tell me. It's a lot scarier in person.
lines.script: [admitting] You did tell me. [rattled] It's a LOT scarier in person.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The man in the mask jumped out! I jumped higher!
lines.script: [defensive] The man in the mask jumped out! [proud of it] I jumped HIGHER!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And it rained popcorn on the whole room. Let's do that to these clouds.
lines.script: [amused, remembering] And it rained popcorn on the whole room. [scheming] Let's do that to these clouds.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don't have any popcorn!
lines.script: [panicking] I don't HAVE any popcorn!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You don't need popcorn. You just need to be that scared.
lines.script: [reassuring] You don't need popcorn. [coaching] You just need to be THAT scared.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oh, I'm that scared.
lines.script: [deadpan, terrified] Oh, I'm that scared.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That doesn't sound like him at all. He tells me how old he is every single morning. He's proud of it!
lines.script: [worried] That doesn't sound like him at all. [fond] He tells me how old he is every single morning. [insisting] He's PROUD of it!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If the smog did this to him, what about everybody on the boulevard?
lines.script: [worried, realizing] If the smog did this to HIM, what about everybody on the boulevard?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Miss Odette and Doña Carmen! Come on!
lines.script: [alarmed] Miss Odette and Doña Carmen! [urging] Come on!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Miss Odette, it's me! Can I get a bowl of gumbo?
lines.script: [cheerful, hopeful] Miss Odette, it's me! [charming] Can I get a bowl of gumbo?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, this is bad. Every time I walk in here she yells "Sit down, you're too skinny!" before the door even closes.
lines.script: [worried] Babe, this is bad. [explaining] Every time I walk in here she yells [imitating her, bossy] "Sit down, you're too SKINNY!" [worried] before the door even closes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Miss Odette? I'm sorry to bother you. TNB is standing up, and he's very skinny today.
lines.script: [overly polite] Miss Odette? I'm sorry to bother you. [baiting her, hopeful] TNB is standing up, and he's VERY skinny today.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nothing. She's just like Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [deflated] Nothing. [worried] She's just like Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, the pupusas are burning!
lines.script: [alarmed] Babe, the pupusas are BURNING!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Doña Carmen, I'm so sorry. I'm coming behind your counter. I know nobody's allowed back here.
lines.script: [apologizing, nervous] Doña Carmen, I'm SO sorry. [announcing, guilty] I'm coming behind your counter. [rushed, apologizing] I know nobody's allowed back here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flipped them. I'm ready for the towel. Go ahead.
lines.script: [reporting] I flipped them. [bracing] I'm ready for the towel. [brave] Go ahead.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She smacks you with that towel if you even look at the griddle.
lines.script: [whispering, awed] She smacks you with that towel if you even LOOK at the griddle.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know! I've never wanted to be hit with a towel so badly!
lines.script: [desperate] I KNOW! [yearning] I've never wanted to be hit with a towel so badly!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The parking tickets can TALK now? They were bad enough when they were quiet!
lines.script: [outraged] The parking tickets can TALK now? [grumbling] They were bad enough when they were quiet!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And I moved my car on Monday night! I set two alarms!
lines.script: [indignant, pleading his case] And I moved my car on Monday night! [nit picky, proud] I set TWO alarms!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Fine. Can I pay it in SkyMiles?
lines.script: [giving up] Fine. [scheming, hopeful] Can I pay it in SkyMiles?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me! She is not a snack. She is our guest!
lines.script: [offended, polite] Excuse me! [correcting] She is NOT a snack. [firm, proper] She is our guest!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We do have snacks, though. I've got half a bag of gummy worms.
lines.script: [helpful, nonchalant] We DO have snacks, though. [offering] I've got half a bag of gummy worms.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Coyotes don't eat gummy worms.
lines.script: [offended, dry] Coyotes don't eat gummy worms.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, look at that tree. It's grey. The leaves, the trunk, even the dirt. It looks like an old black and white movie.
lines.script: [uneasy] Babe, look at that tree. [disbelief] It's GREY. [listing, unsettled] The leaves, the trunk, even the dirt. [awed] It looks like an old black and white movie.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's one lemon on it. And the lemon is inside a block of something orange.
lines.script: [noticing, slowly] There's one lemon on it. [puzzled] And the lemon is inside a block of something... [baffled] orange.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I've seen this before. There's one exactly like it at my parents' pond, with a dragonfly inside.
lines.script: [recognizing, tense] I've seen this before. [serious] There's one EXACTLY like it at my parents' pond, with a dragonfly inside.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: On Long Island? Babe, that's three thousand miles away.
lines.script: [startled] On Long Island? [nonchalant] Babe, that's three thousand miles away.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five.
lines.script: [correcting, automatic] Two thousand four hundred and seventy-five.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's not glass, and it's not glaze. I work with this kind of stuff all day and I have no idea what it is.
lines.script: [investigating] It's not glass, and it's not glaze. [stumped] I work with this kind of stuff all day and I have NO idea what it is.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: There's a little round hole in the side, like somebody took a bite out of it.
lines.script: [investigating] There's a little round hole in the side, [uneasy] like somebody took a bite out of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The one at the pond has the same hole. And you can't pull it off. Rose tried, and then I tried.
lines.script: [informing] The one at the pond has the same hole. [warning] And you can't pull it off. [admitting, sheepish] Rose tried, and then I tried.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Can I try anyway?
lines.script: [undeterred, nonchalant] Can I try anyway?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Wow. Your turn.
lines.script: [stunned] Okay. Wow. [conceding] Your turn.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I already lost to the small one. ...Maybe it's easier in California.
lines.script: [admitting] I already lost to the SMALL one. [hopeful, reasoning] ...Maybe it's easier in California.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's not easier in California.
lines.script: [defeated, flat] It's NOT easier in California.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's a burnt-out flashbulb. My mother found one exactly like it next to the dragonfly.
lines.script: [recognizing, uneasy] It's a burnt-out flashbulb. [serious] My mother found one exactly like it next to the dragonfly.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Who leaves the same bulb at a pond in New York and on a hill in Los Angeles?
lines.script: [puzzling it out] Who leaves the same bulb at a pond in New York... [uneasy] AND on a hill in Los Angeles?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don't know. And I really don't like it.
lines.script: [serious] I don't know. [admitting, quiet] And I REALLY don't like it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Me neither. And I like almost everything.
lines.script: [agreeing, shaken] Me neither. [punchline, deadpan] And I like almost everything.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That hill has EYES! The whole hill just stood up!
lines.script: [shouting, shocked] That hill has EYES! [disbelief] The whole hill just stood up!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. I take naps on that hill.
lines.script: [horrified, hushed] Babe. [confessing] I take NAPS on that hill.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I think you've been napping on his face!
lines.script: [realizing, horrified] I think you've been napping on his FACE!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm so sorry, sir!
lines.script: [mortified, apologizing] I'm SO sorry, sir!

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: RUMBLE. There was a big flash up here this morning, and it woke me up.
lines.script: [deep, rumbling] RUMBLE. [groggy, grumpy] There was a big flash up here this morning, and it woke me up.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: A million years under this city, and everybody up top is always leaving. Today nobody leaves. Not ever.
lines.script: [deep, lonely] A million years under this city, and everybody up top is ALWAYS leaving. [stubborn, firm] Today nobody leaves. [pouting] Not ever.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He'd know. He has four hundred and twelve thousand miles.
lines.script: [dry, vouching for him] He'd know. [sarcastic, fond] He has four hundred and twelve THOUSAND miles.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm sorry I kept falling asleep on you. I didn't know you were a person.
lines.script: [apologizing, sincere] I'm sorry I kept falling asleep on you. [sheepish] I didn't know you were a PERSON.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: I liked the naps. You were the only one who ever stayed.
lines.script: [deep, gentle] I liked the naps. [admitting, lonely] You were the only one who ever stayed.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Something shiny has been stuck in my pipe all day. It tickles. Ah... ah... A-CHOO!
lines.script: [deep, complaining] Something shiny has been stuck in my pipe all day. [ticklish] It TICKLES. [building to a sneeze] Ah... ah... [huge, explosive] A-CHOO!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's a gold coin with a lemon on it. Rose's has a dragonfly.
lines.script: [examining, amazed] It's a gold coin with a LEMON on it. [connecting it] Rose's has a dragonfly.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The one the fish gave her?
lines.script: [checking] The one the FISH gave her?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes. A fish gave her one, and now a hill sneezed one at me.
lines.script: [confirming] Yes. [baffled, tallying] A fish gave her one, and now a hill... [disbelief] SNEEZED one at me.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nara thinks it's a very small frisbee.
lines.script: [amused, observing] Nara thinks it's a very small frisbee.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara, I'm sorry. We don't play fetch with gold.
lines.script: [apologizing to the dog] Nara, I'm sorry. [gently explaining] We don't play fetch with GOLD.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The hill said a flash woke it up this morning. The fish at the pond said the same thing.
lines.script: [thinking out loud] The hill said a flash woke it up this morning. [uneasy, connecting it] The fish at the pond said the SAME thing.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Two flashes, two orange blocks and two gold coins. Babe, I don't love that. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [tallying, slowly] Two flashes, two orange blocks and two gold coins. [understating, uneasy] Babe, I don't love that. [deciding] Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's ten times now. It gets better every time.
lines.script: [fond, amused] That's TEN times now. [sincere] It gets better every time.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: I brought gumbo for the whole block. TNB! Sit DOWN. You're too skinny!
lines.script: [light Louisiana Creole accent, announcing, warm] I brought gumbo for the whole block. [light Louisiana Creole accent, scolding, loud] TNB! Sit DOWN. You're too skinny!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Yes, ma'am!
lines.script: [overjoyed, obedient] YES, ma'am!

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: And YOU. Who went behind my counter?
lines.script: [light Salvadoran accent, stern] And YOU. [light Salvadoran accent, interrogating] Who went behind my counter?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you, Doña Carmen! That's the best towel I've ever been hit with!
lines.script: [overjoyed, grateful] THANK you, Doña Carmen! [sincere, thrilled] That's the best towel I've ever been hit with!

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: They came out perfectly crispy. Don't ever do it again.
lines.script: [light Salvadoran accent, grudgingly impressed] They came out perfectly crispy. [light Salvadoran accent, warning] Don't EVER do it again.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Gumbo. Go get the bread bowl!
lines.script: [excited, realizing] Babe. Gumbo. [urging] Go get the BREAD bowl!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It has a hole in the top. I gave that piece to Nara.
lines.script: [confessing, sheepish] It has a hole in the top. [guilty] I gave that piece to Nara.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's not a hole. That's where the gumbo goes in.
lines.script: [reassuring] That's not a hole. [punchline] That's where the gumbo goes IN.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: With two thousand four hundred and seventy-five miles in between.
lines.script: [tender, wistful] With two thousand four hundred and seventy-five miles in between.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Each way. That's a lot of SkyMiles.
lines.script: [nit picky] Each way. [punchline, content] That's a LOT of SkyMiles.
